Painters, Construction and Maintenance


About the Role
Paint walls, equipment, buildings, bridges, and other structural surfaces, using brushes, rollers, and spray guns. May remove old paint to prepare surface prior to painting. May mix colors or oils to obtain desired color or consistency.
What You'll Do
Cover surfaces with dropcloths or masking tape and paper to protect during painting.
Read work orders or receive instructions from supervisors or homeowners to determine work requirements.
Apply paint, stain, varnish, enamel, or other finishes to equipment, buildings, bridges, or other structures.
Fill cracks, holes, or joints with caulk, putty, plaster, or other fillers.
Smooth surfaces using sandpaper, scrapers, brushes, steel wool, or sanding machines.
Erect scaffolding or swing gates, or set up ladders, to work above ground level.
Apply primers or sealers to prepare new surfaces for finish coats.
Calculate amounts of required materials and estimate costs based on surface measurements.


Tools & Technology
On Center Quick Bid (Project management software)
Microsoft Excel (Spreadsheet software)
Education & Experience
Education: High school diploma or equivalent
On-the-Job Training: 3 to 6 months
Work Environment
Spend time climbing ladders, scaffolds, or poles
High time pressure
Freedom to make decisions
